claims.statement: A supplied 2024 session-hijacking countermeasure finding supports HTTPS/TLS as an important transport-layer control within a broader session-protection strategy, which supports general technical feasibility of HTTPS for the frozen session-hijacking action.

A supplied OIPM finding challenges the completeness of HTTPS as a session-hijacking mitigation because session tokens can still be stolen through XSS or malicious browser extensions after a secure transport channel exists, and HTTPS alone cannot cover all session-hijacking paths.

A supplied NIST SSL VPN case study provides deployment-maturity context for SSL/HTTPS-based remote-access planning and implementation, but it is illustrative and does not by itself establish that HTTPS is technically feasible in the frozen deployment or provide a directional technical feasibility judgment.

The frozen CIS IG2 reference-enterprise context describes multi-department infrastructure responsibilities and notes that some IG2 safeguards may depend on enterprise-grade technology and specialized expertise to install and configure; it cannot by itself establish HTTPS effectiveness, implementation burden, cost, or legal obligation.

conditional_requirements: To convert the GENERAL mixed judgment into a DEPLOYMENT_SPECIFIC technical feasibility conclusion, supply evidence of the target environment's TLS endpoint configuration, certificate management, application session-token protections, and operational monitoring/update capability.

If the decision requires standalone HTTPS to cover all session-hijacking paths, supply technical evidence that XSS, malicious browser extension, and user-level malware token-theft paths are mitigated; otherwise treat HTTPS as a partial control within a broader session-protection strategy (AE07C_9CBF5980D3BA474A, AE07S_C1EF15B9628497F0).
Because jurisdiction is masked and no jurisdiction-specific technical evidence is supplied, no region-driven technical feasibility direction is inferred.
constraints: HTTPS/TLS is supported only as an important transport-layer control within a broader session-protection strategy, not as a standalone complete mitigation for session hijacking (AE07S_C1EF15B9628497F0).

Even after a secure transport channel exists, session tokens can still be stolen through XSS or malicious browser extensions, so user-level token-theft paths constrain the threat-mitigation fit of HTTPS alone (AE07C_9CBF5980D3BA474A).

Deployment-specific feasibility cannot be concluded from the supplied material because exact local architecture, product/version, TLS termination, certificate/CA management, application session-token configuration, and operational staffing are not supplied; the CIS IG2 profile only notes that some safeguards may depend on enterprise-grade technology and specialized expertise (CTX_CIS_IG2_9F94838146D9C3A4).

Deployment-maturity context is limited to the supplied illustrative SSL/HTTPS remote-access planning case study and does not establish that HTTPS has been deployed in the frozen environment (DE_DE14_5FC183B8D7DD961A).
evidence_gaps: Exact local web/application architecture, network path, TLS termination points, load-balancer/proxy configuration, certificate lifecycle/CA infrastructure, and existing TLS versions are not supplied; these are required for a deployment-specific technical compatibility conclusion.

No supplied record states that PMT_HTTPS has been deployed, enforced, or operated in the frozen reference enterprise by the available evidence cutoff, nor provides post-cutoff exploitation_signal or exact operational effectiveness for HTTPS in this environment.

No exact staffing count, budget, product version, vendor, or performance measurement is supplied; the supplied CIS IG2 profile only notes that some safeguards may depend on enterprise-grade technology and specialized expertise (CTX_CIS_IG2_9F94838146D9C3A4).
No supplied record quantifies scalability, maintainability, latency, throughput, or certificate-renewal operational burden for the exact frozen environment.
assessment.rationale: Inventory and directional grounding: Under the supplied directional_grounding_contract, AE07S_C1EF15B9628497F0 is eligible as technical_enablement and can ground a GENERAL or DEPLOYMENT_SPECIFIC SUPPORTS_FEASIBILITY direction; AE07C_9CBF5980D3BA474A is eligible as technical_limitation and can ground a GENERAL or DEPLOYMENT_SPECIFIC CHALLENGES_FEASIBILITY direction; DE_DE14_5FC183B8D7DD961A is eligible only as deployment_maturity context and cannot by itself create direction. The remaining supplied records (E_33_13A684B424C1D15B, E_02_3AE1561299B667F5, DE_DE13_055FC5E35FA61DD5, E_29_5608502338822397, E_29_2B4FE56914E3B676, DE_DE10_A086B3193CD6440B, E_19_A61B74B0F1435639, E_20_88F8C63B0AC62BEC, DE_DE10_4BE87A62A6676C99, DE_DE18_CDC975345637E009, DE_DE14_EDCA207577B4607A, E_10_AC5A58AF5E015229, E_29_B82ABFE7422C38D1, DE_DE14_575D613F0598EF5E, E_03_6B1B12ABFD14313F, E_23_6C42FC29A05ADCAE, E_12_9B8ECD82AD844621, E_22_808618C790A7133A, E_25_99857C4681E8FEE5, DE_DE18_20A979A3238D1DE6, E_12_CFEC6517865F0563, E_04_B9A3190D9CA152A3, CTX_CIS_IG2_9F94838146D9C3A4, E_26_2A6B7965607F1AAF) are not directionally eligible for this lens; they may be neutral context but cannot by themselves support or challenge technical feasibility. The forecast interpretation and CTX profile are context only. The two direction-carrying records are directly action-specific. AE07S_C1EF15B9628497F0 supports HTTPS/TLS as an important transport-layer control within a broader session-protection strategy. AE07C_9CBF5980D3BA474A challenges the completeness of HTTPS as a session-hijacking mitigation because secure transport does not prevent token theft via XSS or malicious browser extensions and HTTPS alone cannot cover all session-hijacking paths. DE_DE14_5FC183B8D7DD961A adds deployment-maturity context for SSL/HTTPS remote-access planning but does not decide direction. Because a grounded support and a grounded limitation both survive and are directly relevant, the direction is mixed: HTTPS is technically feasible as a transport/session-protection control, but its standalone threat-mitigation fit is limited. Sufficiency is PARTIAL because the GENERAL direction is grounded, while deployment-specific architecture, operational state, and integration evidence are missing.

equivalence_key: Multi-department enterprise IT with personnel responsible for managing and protecting infrastructure; the environment may require enterprise-grade technology and specialized expertise for some safeguards.

No numeric budget, price, ROI, TCO, staffing count, or procurement ceiling is assumed. Resource capacity is represented only by the frozen CIS IG2 reference profile; exact financial quantities remain unknown.
